title: Siouxland 8th graders observe Tolerance Week at Violins of Hope - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Prieto-Rivero Maren Ewertz ,
1 hours ago
SIOUX CITY , Iowa ( KCAU ) — As part of an annual tradition, Siouxland 8th graders took part in Tolerance Week . This year, they experienced musical instruments left over from the Holocaust.
“It was an idea that I never planned on,” said Organizer Gerald Weiner.
More than 20 years ago, Weiner, a former Sioux City business owner, learned of a Holocaust survivor raising money to tell his story. Out of his generosity, Weiner donated money and sat down with Holocaust survivor Phillip Gans. Later, starting what is now known as Tolerance Week.
“I listened to this man [Gans] talk for three and a half to four hours… I was moved,” said Weiner. “I had tears. I thought, ‘My God. He has no anger, no bitterness, and he lived through hell in Auschwitz, and he was a death march survivor.'”
Story continues below
In an effort to continue the story and erase the hate, as Gans put it, Weiner made a commitment: reaching out to a retired Sioux City school teacher to help spread the word 21 years ago.
This year, Siouxland students were able to see and listen to instruments used by victims and survivors of the Holocaust at the Orpheum Theater as part of a traveling exhibit called the Violins of Hope .
“It’s a collection of string instruments that were recovered from the concentration camps at the conclusion of the Second World War,” said Executive Director of the Sioux City Symphony Orchestra David S. Gross.
Each instrument carries with it a story.
“We have about 25 instruments here in Sioux City, a collection of about 63 total instruments. All of the violins on stage being played by the Sioux City Symphony musicians are part of that collection,” said Gross.
Weiner hopes the annual event will inspire change.
“We’ve got to get along. There’s an old saying, ‘Mankind’s inhumanity towards mankind.’ My message is how about mankind’s humanity towards mankind,” Weiner said. “We’ve got to make this work, and we will, we will. Good people doing the right things can change the world.”
There will be a free concert on Thursday from 6:30 p.m. to 8 p.m. for those who would like to attend.
